content:
1.  ἄλφα a[lfa a {al&apos;-fah} 
 of Hebrew origin; the first letter of the alphabet; figuratively, only (from its use as a numeral) the first: --Alpha. Often used (usually an, before a vowel) also in composition (as a contraction from 427) in the sense of privation; so, in many words, beginning with this letter; occasionally in the sense of union (as a contraction of 260).  see GREEK for 427  see GREEK for 260

2.  Ἀαρών Ajarwvn Aaron {ah-ar-ohn&apos;} 
 of Hebrew origin (175); Aaron, the brother of Moses:--Aaron.  see HEBREW for 0175

3.  Ἀβαδδών Ajbaddwvn Abaddon {ab-ad-dohn&apos;} 
 of Hebrew origin (11); a destroying angel:--Abaddon.  see HEBREW for 011

4.  ἀβαρής ajbarhvs abares {ab-ar-ace&apos;} 
 from 1 (as a negative particle) and 922; weightless, i.e. (figuratively) not burdensome:--from being burdensome.  see GREEK for 1  see GREEK for 922

5.  αββα abba Abba {ab-bah&apos;} 
 of Chaldee origin (2); father as a vocative:--Abba.  see HEBREW for 02

6.  Ἅβελ A&bel Abel {ab&apos;-el} 
 of Hebrew origin (1893); Abel, the son of Adam:--Abel.  see HEBREW for 01893

7.  Ἀβιά Ajbiav Abia {ab-ee-ah&apos;} 
 of Hebrew origin (29); Abijah, the name of two Israelites:--Abia.  see HEBREW for 029

8.  Ἀβιαθάρ Ajbiaqavr Abiathar {ab-ee-ath&apos;-ar} 
 of Hebrew origin (54); Abiathar, an Israelite:--Abiathar.  see HEBREW for 054

9.  Ἀβιληνή Ajbilhnhv Abilene {ab-ee-lay-nay&apos;} 
 of foreign origin (compare 58); Abilene, a region of Syria:--Abilene.  see HEBREW for 058

10.  Ἀβιούδ Ajbiouvd Abioud {ab-ee-ood&apos;} 
 of Hebrew origin (31); Abihud, an Israelite:--Abiud.  see HEBREW for 031

11.  Ἀβραάμ Ajbraavm Abraam {ab-rah-am&apos;} 
 of Hebrew origin (85); Abraham, the Hebrew patriarch:--Abraham. (In Acts 7:16 the text should probably read Jacob.)  see HEBREW for 085

12.  ἄβυσσος a[bussos abussos {ab&apos;-us-sos} 
 from 1 (as a negative particle) and a variation of 1037; depthless, i.e. (specially) (infernal) &quot;abyss&quot;:--deep, (bottomless) pit.  see GREEK for 1  see GREEK for 1037

13.  Ἅγαβος A&gabos Agabos {ag&apos;-ab-os} 
 of Hebrew origin (compare 2285); Agabus, an Israelite:--Agabus.  see HEBREW for 02285

14.  ἀγαθοεργέω ajgaqoergevw agathoergeo {ag-ath-er-gheh&apos;-o} 
 from 18 and 2041; to work good:--do good.  see GREEK for 18  see GREEK for 2041

15.  ἀγαθοποιέω ajgaqopoievw agathopoieo {ag-ath-op-oy-eh&apos;-o} 
 from 17; to be a well-doer (as a favor or a duty):--(when) do good (well).  see GREEK for 17

16.  ἀγαθοποιΐα ajgaqopoii?a agathopoiia {ag-ath-op-oy-ee&apos;-ah} 
 from 17; well-doing, i.e. virtue:--well-doing.  see GREEK for 17

17.  ἀγαθοποιός ajgaqopoiovs agathopoios {ag-ath-op-oy-os&apos;} 
 from 18 and 4160; a well-doer, i.e. virtuous:--them that do well.  see GREEK for 18  see GREEK for 4160

18.  ἀγαθός ajgaqovs agathos {ag-ath-os&apos;} 
 a primary word; &quot;good&quot; (in any sense, often as noun):--benefit, good(-s, things), well. Compare 2570.  see GREEK for 2570

19.  ἀγαθωσύνη ajgaqwsuvnh agathosune {ag-ath-o-soo&apos;-nay} 
 from 18; goodness, i.e. virtue or beneficence:--goodness.  see GREEK for 18

20.  ἀγαλλίασις ajgallivasis agalliasis {ag-al-lee&apos;-as-is} 
 from 21; exultation; specially, welcome:--gladness, (exceeding) joy.  see GREEK for 21

21.  ἀγαλλιάω ajgalliavw agalliao {ag-al-lee-ah&apos;-o} 
 from agan (much) and 242; properly, to jump for joy, i.e. exult:--be (exceeding) glad, with exceeding joy, rejoice (greatly).  see GREEK for 242

22.  ἄγαμος a[gamos agamos {ag&apos;-am-os} 
 from 1 (as a negative particle) and 1062; unmarried:--unmarried.  see GREEK for 1  see GREEK for 1062

23.  ἀγανακτέω ajganaktevw aganakteo {ag-an-ak-teh&apos;-o} 
 from agan (much) and achthos (grief; akin to the base of 43); to be greatly afflicted, i.e. (figuratively) indignant:--be much (sore) displeased, have (be moved with, with) indignation.  see GREEK for 43

24.  ἀγανάκτησις ajganavkthsis aganaktesis {ag-an-ak&apos;-tay-sis} 
 from 23; indignation:--indignation.  see GREEK for 23

25.  ἀγαπάω ajgapavw agapao {ag-ap-ah&apos;-o} 
 perhaps from agan (much) (or compare 5689); to love (in a social or moral sense):--(be-)love(-ed). Compare 5368.  see GREEK for 5689  see GREEK for 5368

26.  ἀγάπη ajgavph agape {ag-ah&apos;-pay} 
 from 25; love, i.e. affection or benevolence; specially (plural) a love-feast:--(feast of) charity(-ably), dear, love.  see GREEK for 25

27.  ἀγαπητός ajgaphtovs agapetos {ag-ap-ay-tos&apos;} 
 from 25; beloved:--(dearly, well) beloved, dear.  see GREEK for 25

28.  Ἁγάρ AJgavr Hagar {ag&apos;-ar} 
 of Hebrew origin (1904); Hagar, the concubine of Abraham:--Hagar.  see HEBREW for 01904

29.  ἀγγαρεύω ajggareuvw aggareuo {ang-ar-yew&apos;-o} 
 of foreign origin (compare 104); properly, to be a courier, i.e. (by implication) to press into public service:--compel (to go).  see HEBREW for 0104

30.  ἀγγεῖον ἄγγος ajggei&apos;on a[ggos aggeion {ang-eye&apos;-on} 
 from aggos (a pail, perhaps as bent; compare the base of 43); a receptacle:--vessel.  see GREEK for 43

31.  ἀγγελία ajggeliva aggelia {ang-el-ee&apos;-ah} 
 from 32; an announcement, i.e. (by implication) precept:--message.  see GREEK for 32
0031a.  ἀγγέλλω ajggevllw  @@@@0031a

32.  ἄγγελος a[ggelos aggelos {ang&apos;-el-os} 
 from aggello (probably derived from 71; compare 34) (to bring tidings); a messenger; especially an &quot;angel&quot;; by implication, a pastor:--angel, messenger.  see GREEK for 71  see GREEK for 34

33.  ἄγω a[gw age {ag&apos;-eh} 
 imperative of 71; properly, lead, i.e. come on:--go to.  see GREEK for 71

34.  ἀγέλη ajgevlh agele {ag-el&apos;-ay} 
 from 71 (compare 32); a drove:--herd.  see GREEK for 71  see GREEK for 32

35.  ἀγενεαλόγητος ajgenealovghtos agenealogetos {ag-en-eh-al-og&apos;-ay-tos} 
 from 1 (as negative particle) and 1075; unregistered as to birth:--without descent.  see GREEK for 1  see GREEK for 1075

36.  ἀγενής ajgenhvs agenes {ag-en-ace&apos;} 
 from 1 (as negative particle) and 1085; properly, without kin, i.e. (of unknown descent, and by implication) ignoble:--base things.  see GREEK for 1  see GREEK for 1085

37.  ἁγιάζω aJgiavzw hagiazo {hag-ee-ad&apos;-zo} 
 from 40; to make holy, i.e. (ceremonially) purify or consecrate; (mentally) to venerate:--hallow, be holy, sanctify.  see GREEK for 40

38.  ἁγιασμός aJgiasmovs hagiasmos {hag-ee-as-mos&apos;} 
 from 37; properly, purification, i.e. (the state) purity; concretely (by Hebraism) a purifier:--holiness, sanctification.  see GREEK for 37

39.  ἅγιος a&gios hagion {hag&apos;-ee-on} 
 neuter of 40; a sacred thing (i.e. spot):--holiest (of all), holy place, sanctuary.  see GREEK for 40

40.  ἅγιος a&gios hagios {hag&apos;-ee-os} 
 from hagos (an awful thing) (compare 53, 2282); sacred (physically, pure, morally blameless or religious, ceremonially, consecrated):--(most) holy (one, thing), saint.  see GREEK for 53  see GREEK for 2282

41.  ἁγιότης aJgiovths hagiotes {hag-ee-ot&apos;-ace} 
 from 40; sanctity (i.e. properly, the state):--holiness.  see GREEK for 40

42.  ἁγιωσύνη aJgiwsuvnh hagiosune {hag-ee-o-soo&apos;-nay} 
 from 40; sacredness (i.e. properly, the quality):--holiness.  see GREEK for 40

43.  ἀγκάλη ajgkavlh agkale {ang-kal&apos;-ay} 
 from agkos (a bend, &quot;ache&quot;); an arm (as curved):--arm.

44.  ἄγκιστρον a[gkistron agkistron {ang&apos;-kis-tron} 
 from the same as 43; a hook (as bent):--hook.  see GREEK for 43

45.  ἄγκυρα a[gkura agkura {ang&apos;-koo-rah} 
 from the same as 43; an &quot;anchor&quot; (as crooked):--anchor.  see GREEK for 43

46.  ἄγναφος a[gnafos agnaphos {ag&apos;-naf-os} 
 from 1 (as a negative particle) and the same as 1102; properly, unfulled, i.e. (by implication) new (cloth):--new.  see GREEK for 1  see GREEK for 1102

47.  ἁγνεία aJgneiva hagneia {hag-ni&apos;-ah} 
 from 53; cleanliness (the quality), i.e. (specially) chastity:--purity.  see GREEK for 53

48.  ἁγνίζω aJgnivzw hagnizo {hag-nid&apos;-zo} 
 from 53; to make clean, i.e. (figuratively) sanctify (ceremonially or morally):--purify (self).  see GREEK for 53

49.  ἁγνισμός aJgnismovs hagnismos {hag-nis-mos&apos;} 
 from 48; a cleansing (the act), i.e. (ceremonially) lustration:--purification.  see GREEK for 48

50.  ἀγνοέω ajgnoevw agnoeo {ag-no-eh&apos;-o} 
 from 1 (as a negative particle) and 3539; not to know (through lack of information or intelligence); by implication, to ignore (through disinclination):--(be) ignorant(-ly), not know, not understand, unknown.  see GREEK for 1  see GREEK for 3539

51.  ἀγνόημα ajgnovhma agnoema {ag-no&apos;-ay-mah} 
 from 50; a thing ignored, i.e. shortcoming:--error.  see GREEK for 50

52.  ἄγνοια a[gnoia agnoia {ag&apos;-noy-ah} 
 from 50; ignorance (properly, the quality):--ignorance.  see GREEK for 50

53.  ἁγνός aJgnovs hagnos {hag-nos&apos;} 
 from the same as 40; properly, clean, i.e. (figuratively) innocent, modest, perfect:--chaste, clean, pure.  see GREEK for 40

54.  ἁγνότης aJgnovths hagnotes {hag-not&apos;-ace} 
 from 53; cleanness (the state), i.e. (figuratively) blamelessness:--pureness.  see GREEK for 53

55.  ἁγνός aJgnovs hagnos {hag-noce&apos;} 
 adverb from 53; purely, i.e. honestly:--sincerely.  see GREEK for 53

56.  ἀγνωσία ajgnwsiva agnosia {ag-no-see&apos;-ah} 
 from 1 (as negative particle) and 1108; ignorance (properly, the state):--ignorance, not the knowledge.  see GREEK for 1  see GREEK for 1108

57.  ἄγνωστος a[gnwstos agnostos {ag&apos;-noce-tos&apos;} 
 from 1 (as negative particle) and 1110; unknown:--unknown.  see GREEK for 1  see GREEK for 1110

58.  ἀγορά ajgorav agora {ag-or-ah&apos;} 
 from ageiro (to gather; probably akin to 1453); properly, the town-square (as a place of public resort); by implication, a market or thoroughfare:--market(-place), street.  see GREEK for 1453

59.  ἀγοράζω ajgoravzw agorazo {ag-or-ad&apos;-zo} 
 from 58; properly, to go to market, i.e. (by implication) to purchase; specially, to redeem:--buy, redeem.  see GREEK for 58

60.  ἀγοραῖος ajgorai&apos;os agoraios {ag-or-ah&apos;-yos} 
 from 58; relating to the market-place, i.e. forensic (times); by implication, vulgar:--baser sort, low.  see GREEK for 58

61.  ἄγρα a[gra agra {ag&apos;-rah} 
 from 71; (abstractly) a catching (of fish); also (concretely) a haul (of fish):--draught.  see GREEK for 71

62.  ἀγράμματος ajgravmmatos agrammatos {ag-ram-mat-os} 
 from 1 (as negative particle) and 1121; unlettered, i.e. illiterate:--unlearned.  see GREEK for 1  see GREEK for 1121

63.  ἀγραυλέω ajgraulevw agrauleo {ag-row-leh&apos;-o} 
 from 68 and 832 (in the sense of 833); to camp out:--abide in the field.  see GREEK for 68  see GREEK for 832  see GREEK for 833

64.  ἀγρεύω ajgreuvw agreuo {ag-rew&apos;-o} 
 from 61; to hunt, i.e. (figuratively) to entrap:--catch.  see GREEK for 61

65.  ἀγριέλαιος ajgrievlaios agrielaios {ag-ree-el&apos;-ah-yos} 
 from 66 and 1636; an oleaster:--olive tree (which is) wild.  see GREEK for 66  see GREEK for 1636

66.  ἄγριος a[grios agrios {ag&apos;-ree-os} 
 from 68; wild (as pertaining to the country), literally (natural) or figuratively (fierce):--wild, raging.  see GREEK for 68

67.  Ἀγρίππας Ajgrivppas Agrippas {ag-rip&apos;-pas} 
 apparently from 66 and 2462; wild-horse tamer; Agrippas, one of the Herods:--Agrippa.  see GREEK for 66  see GREEK for 2462

68.  ἀγρός ajgrovs agros {ag-ros&apos;} 
 from 71; a field (as a drive for cattle); genitive case, the country; specially, a farm, i.e. hamlet:--country, farm, piece of ground, land.  see GREEK for 71

69.  ἀγρυπνέω ajgrupnevw agrupneo {ag-roop-neh&apos;-o} 
 ultimately from 1 (as negative particle) and 5258; to be sleepless, i.e. keep awake:--watch.  see GREEK for 1  see GREEK for 5258

70.  ἀγρυπνία ajgrupniva agrupnia {ag-roop-nee&apos;-ah} 
 from 69; sleeplessness, i.e. a keeping awake:--watch.  see GREEK for 69

71.  ἄγω a[gw ago {ag&apos;-o} 
 a primary verb; properly, to lead; by implication, to bring, drive, (reflexively) go, (specially) pass (time), or (figuratively) induce:--be, bring (forth), carry, (let) go, keep, lead away, be open.

72.  ἀγωγή ajgwghv agoge {ag-o-gay&apos;} 
 reduplicated from 71; a bringing up, i.e. mode of living:--manner of life.  see GREEK for 71

73.  ἀγών ajgwvn agon {ag-one&apos;} 
 from 71; properly, a place of assembly (as if led), i.e. (by implication) a contest (held there); figuratively, an effort or anxiety:--conflict, contention, fight, race.  see GREEK for 71

74.  ἀγωνία ajgwniva agonia {ag-o-nee&apos;-ah} 
 from 73; a struggle (properly, the state), i.e. (figuratively) anguish:--agony.  see GREEK for 73

75.  ἀγωνίζομαι ajgwnivzomai agonizomai {ag-o-nid&apos;-zom-ahee} 
 from 73; to struggle, literally (to compete for a prize), figuratively (to contend with an adversary), or genitive case (to endeavor to accomplish something):--fight, labor fervently, strive.  see GREEK for 73

76.  Ἀδάμ Ajdavm Adam {ad-am&apos;} 
 of Hebrew origin (121); Adam, the first man; typically (of Jesus) man (as his representative):--Adam.  see HEBREW for 0121

77.  ἀδάπανος ajdavpanos adapanos {ad-ap&apos;-an-os} 
 from 1 (as negative particle); and 1160; costless, i.e. gratuitous:--without expense.  see GREEK for 1  see GREEK for 1160

78.  Ἀδδί Ajddiv Addi {ad-dee&apos;} 
 probably of Hebrew origin (compare 5716); Addi, an Israelite:--Addi.  see HEBREW for 05716

79.  ἀδελφή ajdelfhv adelphe {ad-el-fay&apos;} 
 fem of 80; a sister (naturally or ecclesiastically):--sister.  see GREEK for 80

80.  ἀδελφός ajdelfovs adelphos {ad-el-fos&apos;} 
 from 1 (as a connective particle) and delphus (the womb); a brother (literally or figuratively) near or remote (much like 1):--brother.  see GREEK for 1  see GREEK for 1

81.  ἀδελφότης ajdelfovths adelphotes {ad-el-fot&apos;-ace} 
 from 80; brotherhood (properly, the feeling of brotherliness), i.e. the (Christian) fraternity:--brethren, brotherhood.  see GREEK for 80

82.  ἄδηλος a[dhlos adelos {ad&apos;-ay-los} 
 from 1 (as a negative particle) and 1212; hidden, figuratively, indistinct:--appear not, uncertain.  see GREEK for 1  see GREEK for 1212

83.  ἄδηλος a[dhlos adelotes {ad-ay-lot&apos;-ace} 
 from 82; uncertainty:--X uncertain.  see GREEK for 82

84.  ἀδήλως ajdhvlws adelos {ad-ay&apos;-loce} 
 adverb from 82; uncertainly:--uncertainly.  see GREEK for 82

85.  ἀδημονέω ajdhmonevw ademoneo {ad-ay-mon-eh&apos;-o} 
 from a derivative of adeo (to be sated to loathing); to be in distress (of mind):--be full of heaviness, be very heavy.

86.  ᾅδης a&/dhs hades {hah&apos;-dace} 
 from 1 (as negative particle) and 1492; properly, unseen, i.e. &quot;Hades&quot; or the place (state) of departed souls:--grave, hell.  see GREEK for 1  see GREEK for 1492

87.  ἀδιάκριτος ajdiavkritos adiakritos {ad-ee-ak&apos;-ree-tos} 
 from 1 (as a negative particle) and a derivative of 1252; properly, undistinguished, i.e. (actively) impartial:--without partiality.  see GREEK for 1  see GREEK for 1252

88.  ἀδιάλειπτος ajdiavleiptos adialeiptos {ad-ee-al&apos;-ipe-tos} 
 from 1 (as a negative particle) and a derivative of a compound of 1223 and 3007; unintermitted, i.e. permanent:--without ceasing, continual.  see GREEK for 1  see GREEK for 1223  see GREEK for 3007

89.  ἀδιαλείπτως ajdialeivptws adialeiptos {ad-ee-al-ipe&apos;-toce} 
 adverb from 88; uninterruptedly, i.e. without omission (on an appropriate occasion):--without ceasing.  see GREEK for 88

90.  ἀφθορία ajfqoriva adiaphthoria {ad-ee-af-thor-ee&apos;-ah} 
 from a derivative of a compound of 1 (as a negative particle) and a derivative of 1311; incorruptibleness, i.e. (figuratively) purity (of doctrine):--uncorruptness.  see GREEK for 1  see GREEK for 1311

91.  ἀδικέω ajdikevw adikeo {ad-ee-keh&apos;-o} 
 from 94; to be unjust, i.e. (actively) do wrong (morally, socially or physically):--hurt, injure, be an offender, be unjust, (do, suffer, take) wrong.  see GREEK for 94

92.  ἀδίκημα ajdivkhma adikema {ad-eek&apos;-ay-mah} 
 from 91; a wrong done:--evil doing, iniquity, matter of wrong.  see GREEK for 91

93.  ἀδικία ajdikiva adikia {ad-ee-kee&apos;-ah} 
 from 94; (legal) injustice (properly, the quality, by implication, the act); morally, wrongfulness (of character, life or act):--iniquity, unjust, unrighteousness, wrong.  see GREEK for 94

94.  ἄδικος a[dikos adikos {ad&apos;-ee-kos} 
 from 1 (as a negative particle) and 1349; unjust; by extension wicked; by implication, treacherous; specially, heathen:--unjust, unrighteous.  see GREEK for 1  see GREEK for 1349

95.  ἀδίκως ajdivkws adikos {ad-ee&apos;-koce} 
 adverb from 94; unjustly:--wrongfully.  see GREEK for 94

96.  ἀδόκιμος ajdovkimos adokimos {ad-ok&apos;-ee-mos} 
 from 1 (as a negative particle) and 1384; unapproved, i.e. rejected; by implication, worthless (literally or morally):--castaway, rejected, reprobate.  see GREEK for 1  see GREEK for 1384

97.  ἄδολος a[dolos adolos {ad&apos;-ol-os} 
 from 1 (as a negative particle}; and 1388; undeceitful, i.e. (figuratively) unadulterated:--sincere.  see GREEK for 1  see GREEK for 1388

98.  Ἁδραμυττηνός Ἀδραμυττηνός  AJdramutthnovs Ajdramutthnovs Adramuttenos {ad-ram-oot-tay-nos&apos;} 
 from Adramutteion (a place in Asia Minor); Adramyttene or belonging to Adramyttium:--of Adramyttium.

99.  Ἀδρίας Ajdrivas Adrias {ad-ree&apos;-as} 
 from Adria (a place near its shore); the Adriatic sea (including the Ionian):--Adria.

100.  ἁδρότης aJdrovths hadrotes {had-rot&apos;-ace} 
 from hadros (stout); plumpness, i.e. (figuratively) liberality:--abundance.

101.  ἀδυνατέω ajdunatevw adunateo {ad-oo-nat-eh&apos;-o} 
 from 102; to be unable, i.e. (passively) impossible:--be impossible.  see GREEK for 102

102.  ἀδύνατος ajduvnatos adunatos {ad-oo&apos;-nat-os} 
 from 1 (as a negative particle) and 1415; unable, i.e. weak (literally or figuratively); passively, impossible:--could not do, impossible, impotent, not possible, weak.  see GREEK for 1  see GREEK for 1415

104.  ἀεί ajeiv aei {ah-eye&apos;} 
 from an obsolete primary noun (apparently meaning continued duration); &quot;ever,&quot;by qualification regularly; by implication, earnestly; --always, ever.

105.  ἀετός ajetovs aetos {ah-et-os&apos;} 
 from the same as 109; an eagle (from its wind-like flight):--eagle.  see GREEK for 109

106.  ἄζυμος a[zumos azumos {ad&apos;-zoo-mos} 
 from 1 (as a negative particle) and 2219; unleavened, i.e. (figuratively) uncorrupted; (in the neutral plural) specially (by implication) the Passover week:--unleavened (bread).  see GREEK for 1  see GREEK for 2219

107.  Ἀζώρ Ajzwvr Azor {ad-zore&apos;} 
 of Hebrew origin (compare 5809); Azor, an Israelite:--Azorigin  see HEBREW for 05809

108.  Ἄζωτος A[zwtos Azotos {ad&apos;-zo-tos} 
 of Hebrew origin (795); Azotus (i.e. Ashdod), a place in Palestine:--Azotus.  see HEBREW for 0795

109.  ἀήρ ajhvr aer {ah-ayr&apos;} 
 from aemi (to breathe unconsciously, i.e. respire; by analogy, to blow); &quot;air&quot; (as naturally circumambient):--air. Compare 5594.  see GREEK for 5594

110.  ἀθανασία ajqanasiva athanasia {ath-an-as-ee&apos;-ah} 
 from a compound of 1 (as a negative particle) and 2288; deathlessness:--immortality.  see GREEK for 1  see GREEK for 2288

111.  ἀθέμιτος ajqevmitos athemitos {ath-em&apos;-ee-tos} 
 from 1 (as a negative particle) and a derivative of themis (statute; from the base of 5087); illegal; by implication, flagitious:--abominable, unlawful thing.  see GREEK for 1  see GREEK for 5087

112.  ἄθεος a[qeos atheos {ath&apos;-eh-os} 
 from 1 (as a negative particle) and 2316; godless:--without God.  see GREEK for 1  see GREEK for 2316

113.  ἄθεσμος a[qesmos athesmos {ath&apos;-es-mos} 
 from 1 (as a negative particle) and a derivative of 5087 (in the sense of enacting); lawless, i.e. (by implication) criminal:--wicked.  see GREEK for 1  see GREEK for 5087

114.  ἀθετέω ajqetevw atheteo {ath-et-eh&apos;-o} 
 from a compound of 1 (as a negative particle) and a derivative of 5087; to set aside, i.e. (by implication) to disesteem, neutralize or violate:--cast off, despise, disannul, frustrate, bring to nought, reject.  see GREEK for 1  see GREEK for 5087

115.  ἀθέτησις ajqevthsis athetesis {ath-et&apos;-ay-sis} 
 from 114; cancellation (literally or figuratively):--disannulling, put away.  see GREEK for 114
